figures.caption: Figure 1: Overview of the proposed method. A mask, M , of the same dimensions as the time-frequency representation, g(x), is initialised randomly. An explanation is then the product of a learning problem tied to the mask using an objective function that enforces sparsity, smoothness and consistency between the original prediction of the model and the prediction of the masked input, g−1(g(x) ◦M).
Figure 2: Illustration of the difference between the three representations on 15 second from the SleepEDF dataset (Goldberger et al., 2000; Kemp et al., 2000).
Table 1: Hyperparameters for XACT for all representations. For the synthetic data we only used non-masked STDFT and the sweep results in the following parameters: r = 0.01, λ1 = 5 and λ2 = 1.

Figure 3: An example of a synthetic datapoint with the ground truth tone overlaid in green. Explanations for the three different methods are provided. The explanation provided by XACT is much more exact than those of FreqRISE and LRP with no highlights of the spurious frequencies.

Figure 4: Explanation for a sample from SleepEDF belonging to the class of REM sleep. The time series itself is plotted in red on top of the representations with some smoothing to avoid too much jitter in the visualisation. Its y-axis is arbitrary. FreqRISE and XACT have been masked for energy. The CWT is plotted with a linear y-scale for easier comparison to the other representations, but with the consequence that the high frequencies are stretched vertically.

Figure 5: Faithfulness for different quantiles for the three different methods for both datasets and STDFT representation where FreqRISE and XACT have been masked for energy. Accuracy of the SleepEDF model is 80% where we can see FreqRISE overshoots.

Table 3: Explanation metrics on AudioMNIST. The upper numbers are the metrics on the unmasked runs, and the lower one is the changed masking does to it reported as an index. Masking thus improved the metric when the index is above than 100% except for FI where it is the opposite. Note the confidence around R is not symmetric as we have computed the log of the standard deviation.
